newsitem.title: UK: SMITHS, ENGINEERS GAIN ON SOFT STERLING.
newsitem.headline: SMITHS, ENGINEERS GAIN ON SOFT STERLING.

text.p: Shares in Smiths Industries Plc led the engineering sector sharply higher on Friday as a weaker sterling alleviated fears over the hit to overseas earnings, market sources said.
Pleasing results from GKN Plc on Wednesday, in the face of a stronger sterling in the first half of the year, continued to underpin the sector as well.
By 0857 GMT, Smiths shares gained 38p or 4.6 percent to 871-1/2p, hitting a record high 875p, and GKN rose 31-1/2p to 12.19 stg, bucking a sell-off in the FTSE 100.
TI Group shares rose 20-1/2p to 614p, Siebe jumped 21-1/2p to 11.47 stg and Glynwed Plc 13-1/2p to 262p.
"The GKN results proved that some larger international companies with local production may not get hit as bad some people assume," one analyst said.

"Coupled with sterling coming off, the outlook looks a lot better," he said. "The sector was so heavily influenced adversely by the currency movement, when the currency comes back the other way it should have the opposite effect."

Sterling tumbled on Thursday and was below the key three-mark level on Friday, after the Bank of England hiked rates by 25 basis points to 7.0 percent and signalled that rates may hold steady for the time being.

Weaker sterling helps companies when they translate their overseas earnings back into the British currency, the analyst said. But some companies are protected from sterling's rise due to local production, he said.

GKN on Wednesday unveiled a 12.2 percent rise in half-year profits to 203 million pounds. Analysts said current year forecasts of around 385 million pounds pre-tax were likely to be raised to 400 million pounds, up from last year's 362.8 million.
